title: Multiband and multichannel pairing
summary: A coupling matrix determines a pairing instability. Multiple bands, interaction channels, transport channels and material phases are different concepts.

claims.statement: Multiband pairing concerns how superconducting gaps on distinct bands are coupled. Multichannel pairing concerns different interaction contributions to a Cooper-pair kernel. Neither concept is equivalent to parallel normal-state electrical conductivities, and neither means that two spatially separate superconducting phases form one homogeneous condensate. Keeping these distinctions explicit prevents apparent evidence for several channels from becoming an unsupported mechanism claim.
claims.conditions: The common-cutoff equation is a weak-coupling illustration in a declared band basis. Real spectra, self-energy, Coulomb terms and interband scattering need an explicit kernel.
claims.verificationScope: The Choi source identity is corrected; its selected MgB2 calculation does not independently establish every general statement in this paragraph. Broader claim-level primary support remains pending.

claims.statement: In this declared approximation, the largest relevant pairing eigenvalue sets the instability. Off-diagonal entries represent interband pair transfer and help constrain relative gap phases. A matrix eigenvalue is not the arithmetic sum of all its entries. The energy cutoff notation here makes the dimensions explicit when converting the original ASCII equation.

claims.statement: The full problem can have different frequency spectra, momentum structure, repulsive terms, Coulomb effects and normal self-energy renormalization. Combining a pairing attraction and a mass enhancement into one positive scalar can give a misleading temperature estimate. Interactions can cooperate, compete or favor different gap structures after projection into the pairing channel.

claims.statement: Choi and colleagues calculated band-dependent gaps in MgB2 using an anisotropic Eliashberg treatment of electron-phonon pairing. Their sigma- and pi-band gaps vanish at a common calculated transition temperature. This is a theoretical result consistent with multiple gaps within that model; it is not a direct measurement of two independent pairing mediators.
claims.conditions: Band-resolved anisotropic Eliashberg calculation for MgB2 with its electron-phonon model; not an experimental determination of separate pairing glues or a universal result for all multiband materials.
claims.verificationScope: Choi et al., Nature 418, 758-760 (2002), pp. 758-759 and Fig. 3. Selected model/result passages checked, not independent numerical reproduction.

claims.statement: In single-layer FeSe/SrTiO3, replica-band observations support the relevance of an interface electron-phonon interaction. They do not independently extract every spin, interface and plasmon contribution as a set of additive coupling constants. The interface hypothesis must be tested together with charge transfer, the reconstructed electronic structure and phase-coherence limitations.

claims.statement: A high pairing or gap-closing scale measured by ARPES is not automatically a zero-resistance transition. When an interface and intrinsic electronic interactions are both discussed, the useful object is a specified combined kernel with assumptions and uncertainties. This pilot deliberately contains no unsourced table of separate FeSe/SrTiO3 coupling constants.

claims.statement: A common transition temperature is compatible with interband locking, but does not establish beneficial synergy between distinct interactions. Changes in a band structure, density of states or scattering rate can alter the instability without revealing a unique mediator. Cross-material percentages assigned to a plasmon enhancement are not universal physical constants.

claims.statement: A testable multichannel proposal predicts a gap structure and its response to an independent control parameter. Show what would distinguish cooperation from competition, and check that the same interaction has not been counted twice. The most useful next measurement constrains a specific matrix element or spectral contribution rather than simply adding another possible mechanism to a list.
